characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/max-2500 instrument at 40 kV, scanning 30°–100° at 4°/min
characterization_methods.key_findings: Microstructure consists of ferrite (δ) and austenite (γ); diffraction peak intensity shows almost no significant change after aging.
Irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed in the austenite matrix; ferrite content 18.3 vol% at 823 K/3 h; submicron white NbC particles present.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: samples electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution at 25 V for 10 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize microstructure morphology and measure ferrite content

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apollo 300 SEM equipped with an EBSD detector; scanning step size 300 nm; Channel 5 software; grain boundaries identified by minimum misorientation angle of 15°
characterization_methods.key_findings: Austenite grain size ≈18 µm (unchanged from as-cast) for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h; fragmented microstructure with many small equiaxed regions.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine grain size and grain morphology

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JEM-2100 TEM operating at 200 kV; double-jet electropolishing with 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol at ≈30 °C and 35 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: Large amount of nano-scale κ-carbides dispersed in austenite; κ-carbide volume fraction 27.8 vol% and average size 7.8 nm at 823 K/3 h; coherent relationship [100]γ//[100]κ.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize nano-scale κ-carbides and NbC precipitates

characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite content 18.3 vol%; κ-carbide average size 7.8 nm at 823 K/3 h.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: more than five SEM images per sample for ferrite content; multiple clear TEM DF regions for κ-carbide size
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure ferrite content, NbC size/volume fraction and κ-carbide size

characterization_methods.key_findings: 467 HV for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s

characterization_methods.key_findings: Yield strength 1041 ± 15 MPa, tensile strength 1125 ± 10 MPa, total elongation 8 ± 3 %.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm; minimum four repetitions

analytical_models.model_note: Calculated dislocation strengthening in austenite = 40.2 MPa for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
Calculated grain boundary strengthening = 88.6 MPa for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
Calculated κ-carbide precipitation strengthening = 274.8 MPa for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
Calculated NbC Orowan strengthening = 4.7 MPa for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.
Calculated ferrite dislocation strengthening = 93.3 MPa for the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Uses experimental inputs: austenite grain size ≈18 µm, austenite dislocation density 1.48 × 10^13 m^-2, ferrite dislocation density 1.04 × 10^15 m^-2, κ-carbide size 7.8 nm and volume fraction 27.8 vol%, NbC size and volume fraction, and austenite volume fraction >80 vol%.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated contributions are used to explain the measured yield-strength increase after aging.

analytical_models.model_note: Formation energies: Fe24Al8C8 = 0.891 eV; Fe23NbAl8C8 = 2.826 eV; Fe24Al7NbC8 = 1.453 eV. Nb doping significantly increases the κ-carbide formation energy.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: plane-wave cutoff 500 eV; Gaussian smearing 0.05 eV; energy convergence <0.03 eV/Å; vacuum spacing 15 Å; 6 × 6 × 6 Monkhorst–Pack k-point sampling; 2 × 2 × 2 supercell of κ-carbide (Fe3AlC, E21).
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: PAW potentials; U scheme with U = 2.59 eV for Fe
computational_details.simulation_method: spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) within GGA-PBE

analytical_models.model_note: NbC (MC) precipitation temperature increases from ≈973 K to 1573 K as Nb content increases from 0 to 0.05 wt%; Nb content has limited impact on the liquid-to-solid transformation temperature.

analytical_models.model_name: C and Al diffusion in austenite
analytical_models.model_note: Nb slightly decreases the diffusion coefficient of C in austenite (strong Nb–C affinity) and slightly increases Al diffusion; the slower C diffusion decelerates κ-carbide nucleation and growth.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: temperature range 673–873 K; Al and C diffusion in austenite for the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Nano-scale κ-carbides are sheared by dislocations under plastic deformation; strengthening quantified with N = 6 and γ_APB = 350 mJ m^-2.
Large-size NbC particles are impermeable and strengthen by the Orowan looping mechanism (Ashby–Orowan equation).

interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging at 823 K for 3 h increases κ-carbide volume fraction (3.3 → 27.8 vol%) and average size (2.0 → 7.8 nm) while the austenite grain size remains almost unchanged; no coarsened intergranular κ-carbides are observed.

phase_interfaces.coherence: irregular phase boundaries; no coherency reported

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield strength of 0.04Nb steel (823 K/3 h) = 1056 MPa versus 0.02Nb steel (823 K/3 h) = 1041 MPa; overall the 0.04Nb steels exceed the 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa in yield strength.

processing_steps.method: induction melting followed by centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Steel strips with dimensions 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm were obtained through near-rapid solidification.
Aging treatment of the as-cast (near-rapid solidified) steel strips at 823 K for 3 h.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: each steel strip underwent a minimum of four repetitions
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve (green, 823 K/3 h) reaches the highest stress (~1100–1200 MPa) but terminates at the smallest strain (~8 %).

samples.sample_label: 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K for 3 h

phases_present.morphology: irregular-shaped, randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix

precipitates.distribution: intragranular; volume fraction 27.8 vol%; large amount of nano-scale κ-carbides dispersed in austenite
submicron white particles within the austenite matrix; volume fraction ≈0.6 vol% (read from Figure 4 gridlines)

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase microstructure consisting of an austenite (γ) matrix with irregular-shaped ferrite (δ) randomly dispersed within it; intragranular nano-scale κ-carbides and submicron NbC particles are present in the austenite.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 0.02Nb steel strip (Table 1): Mn 12.80, Al 9.01, Cr 3.01, C 1.39, Nb 0.021, Fe Bal. (wt%).
Measured chemical composition of austenite in the 0.02Nb steel (Table 4): Mn 13.12, Al 8.35, Cr 4.06, C 1.39, Nb 0.019, Fe 63.79 wt%.
No coarsened intergranular κ-carbides were detected after aging treatment at 723–823 K.
Austenite accounts for over 80 vol% of the microstructure and plays a dominant role in determining the mechanical properties of the low-density steel.
Ferrite grain size of the as-cast 0.02Nb steel is 3.6 µm; the specific ferrite grain size for the 823 K/3 h state is not explicitly reported.
For the 0.02Nb steel aged at 823 K, yield strength increases from 880 MPa (as-cast) to 1041 MPa while total elongation decreases from 39% to 8%.
For Nb-containing steels aged at temperatures exceeding 773 K, the precipitation of κ-carbide is the principal strengthening factor.
